A status is one of: measured, not-observed (the check ran, its control passed, and it saw nothing), not-run (the check did not run, or its control failed, so it says nothing) or static reading (read locally from the game, never measured). The decision value is the research doc's Decision key as recorded; each entry's checks carry their tools/live_checks.py verdicts. Addresses and call-site offsets are never recorded here; the callers are named. Static readings are our own words, never the game's text.

speed_lever.what: x0.5 on id 64's result at the dispatcher, on every call for 240 frames, slowed the walk's step to 0.785 of itself, not 0.5. The lever scaled only the dispatcher's answer: skip=240 means every local StatMovementSpeed call inside the dispatcher returned a non-number to the probe, so the getter route never scaled (changed_getter 0), against the probe core's tested model. Halving the dispatcher's id-64 answer gave 0.785 of the step. Whether the step is not proportional to it (base, cap, floor), whether the walk also reads movement speed by a route the dispatcher lever does not reach (e.g. the cached pSt values PlayerMovement reads), and why the getter's own result was not a number to the probe (skip=240) are not established. ss_check.what: The draw's tier-5 test on protected value slot 75. A pushed SS stand-in is rarely built through the draw: 2 SS stand-ins built among 105 draw builds at magic find x10 (Live 1c), 0 among 6 at x1 (Live 1b; not pooled), against about 0.3 of draws expected if the draw kept the first entry it reads (s*c = 100 copies on lists of about 221 entries). Why SS stand-ins are rarely built is not established. The probe's picks= (47 in Live 1c, 13 in Live 1b) is an instrument count, not the draw's picks: it counts any CreateDefaultParams call in the draw's scope whose sub and b match a pushed triple read since the read window was last cleared, it does not compare the class, and a normal build does not clear the window. The debugger logpoint on the draw's own CreateDefaultParams call hit 105 times, equal to the 105 draw builds and including both stand-ins, so the other 45 counted calls ran at another call site; they are not the draw picking a stand-in and sending it back. Both slot-75 read sites were reached (at least 3.1 and 1.57 hits a call; the log condition's literals were read as hex, so counts resolve to 512) and every logged hit carried 75.0, a real, as the logpoint's logged value (139 lines). Whether that is the index argument or the value stored in slot 75 is not established, and the comparison after the read was not logged, so whether the tier-5 test rejects anything is not established either. No natural rarity-6 tier-5 unique was built through the draw in 28 minutes at x10; natural tier-5 draw builds came at k = 5 with rarity 7 (1, the owner calls it Angelic) and rarity 9 (2, Heroic). Aimbot.exe (class 10, base 76, rarity 6, tier 5) was built 8 times in scope outside.
